key_insight: MCTS can waste exploration on differently worded versions of the same reasoning strategy; learned pseudo-counts let related branches share exploration evidence.
engineering_relevance: Changing only UCT’s exploration statistic offers a targeted way to improve LLM reasoning search without redesigning the full search algorithm.
method: Identify how fragmented branch visit counts can increase cumulative regret.
Estimate representation coverage with a lightweight Coin-Flipping Network head on policy hidden states.
Use learned pseudo-counts in UCT to share exploration evidence across related branches.
evidence_signal: Across 5 mathematical-reasoning and 7 search benchmarks, LPC-MCTS outperformed strong MCTS baselines; with trained policies held fixed, inference-time count replacement improved average mean@16 math accuracy by 3.79 percentage points on Qwen2.5-7B and 2.71 on Qwen3-4B.
watch_item: Coverage estimates depend on learned representations; the abstract does not quantify the head’s computational overhead or robustness to misleading branch similarity.
paper_title: MCTS Is Counting the Wrong Thing: Learning Exploration Counts for LLM Reasoning
